Choosing a Contractor
How do I choose a remodeling contractor?

The best contractors get work through satisfied customers’ referrals not from the biggest ads in the paper. Consult friends and neighbors who have had work done and ask for a referral.

Also consult the Better Business Bureau and Angie’s List for reviews of the contractors you’re considering. Be wary of a contractor with more than two or three negative reviews or complaints.

Ensure that your contractor is licensed. Licensing won’t guarantee success, but it does indicate a degree of professionalism and suggests that the contractor is committed to his or her job. The same holds true for membership in, or certification by, an industry group such as the National Association of the Remodeling Industry (NARI) and the NAHB Remodeling Council.

Ask to see a current Certificate of Insurance, so that you can see that the contractor has both General Liability and Worker’s Compensation coverage. Everyone say’s “fully insured,” but many are not.

No matter how you find potential contractors, be sure to ask for a list of previous customers that you can call for referrals. Then call them and, if possible, visit their homes to look at the work. Ask specific questions such as:

Would you hire this contractor again?
Were you satisfied with the quality of the work?
How did the contractor handle cleanup each day?
How did the contractor handle differences and work changes?
Was the job completed on time and at the bid price? If not, why not?
Were the contractors and staff knowledgeable, friendly and helpful? Were they quick to respond to any questions or concerns you may have had?

You might also ask the contractor for a list of his or her building-material suppliers. Call them to see if the contractor has an account or pays for items upon delivery. Most suppliers are willing to extend credit to financially reliable contractors.

*Attention: Federal law requires that we present you with the “Lead-Safe Certified Guide to Renovate Right”. Click here to read the booklet. Paper booklets are available upon request.

How do I spot a questionable contractor?

A warning signal should sound in your head if you encounter any of the following:

High-pressure sales tactics or threats to rescind a special price if you don’t sign on the spot.
A contractor who tries to scare you into signing a contract by claiming that your house puts you at peril (i.e., “Your electrical wiring could start a fire if it isn’t replaced.”)
A contractor who makes unsolicited phone calls or visits. Be especially wary of people who offer a bargain price, claiming that they’re doing a job in the neighborhood and have leftover materials.
A contractor whose address can’t be verified, who uses only a post office box, or who has only an answering service and no separate listing in the telephone book.
A contractor who isn’t affiliated with any recognized trade association.
License or insurance information you can’t verify.
A contractor who can’t (or won’t) provide references for similar jobs in your area.
The promise of a hefty discount—but no mention of the total cost of the job.
The promise of a deep discount if the contractor uses your home as a “demo.”

 

All contractors say “fully insured” but what does that mean?

Contractors should carry General Liability, Worker’s Compensation, NYS Disability, Vehicle and Builder’s Risk Insurances. Advertising claims are not good insurance; to be sure your contractor has current, paid-up insurance ask to see a Certificate of Insurance. These are an official statement of coverage, produced by the contractor’s insurance company. It is common for customers to ask for these and any good contractor will be able to provide one within days.

Bathrooms
Why should I choose a full service bathroom remodeler?

A full service remodeler like Bennett, will take care of all the preliminary steps involved in designing and creating your new bathroom from design and planning, to securing building codes and permits and scheduling.

Bennett’s full service remodeling will also guide you through the process of choosing the right materials for the job. Bennett partners with various local suppliers who have showrooms, samples and National Kitchen & Bath Association (NKBA) certified designers.  A bathroom may be small, but it includes many choices:

Plumbing fixtures, tub, sink, faucet and accessories
Cabinets, mirrors, countertops
Design & install of tile, marble and ceramic materials
Shower door installation
Lighting & heating design
Painting, wainscoting and wall paper design

With 100 years of experience, and thousands of completed jobs from handicap accessible to custom spa designs, Bennett can advise you each step of the way. Our licensed plumbers and electricians on staff work efficiently, meeting all the local codes and inspector requirements.

What are the pros and cons of acrylic bath liners?

The Advantages

1. Buying an acrylic bathtub liner and surround is easy. You can find lots of companies that will install an acrylic bathtub liner in your bathroom.

2. No demolition necessary if you choose an acrylic bathtub liner. This is the leading reason for having an acrylic bathtub liner and surround installed. The liner goes in the old tub.

3. The actual installation can be completely done in one day. On the other hand, replacing a bathtub and remodeling your bathroom can take several days.

The Disadvantages

1. A tub liner hides the problems, but doesn’t solve them. Water damaged walls, mold, rusty pipes, slow drains, inadequate wiring, get covered up by the liner and lots of caulk.

2. An acrylic bathtub is narrower and the sides are higher. Since it’s a tub in a tub, acrylic bathtub liners make your original tub two or three inches narrower and higher which makes it harder to reach into. It’s more difficult to clean the tub, bathe the kids, hand wash clothing, etc.

3. When you are done, it’s the “same old bathroom”. If your goal is to improve your overall bathroom appearance, create a safer, cleaner more comfortable place with better lighting, tile floors, shower seats, grab bars, big mirrors, warm floors and more then a simple acrylic liner may not be the right choice.

Conclusion

If you are looking for a “quick fix” the tub insert is quick and easy. If you want 20 years of quality and comfort in a newly designed bathroom then consider a remodel that will redesign layouts, update fixtures, replace the plumbing and wiring if needed and create a whole new bathroom experience. Contact a full service bathroom expert like Bennett Contracting for a free consultation.

Kitchens
What should I expect from a quality kitchen contractor?

When you choose a full service remodeler like Bennett, all the steps involved in creating your new kitchen from design and planning to building code and installation requirements, are professionally handled by experienced project managers and contractors. Bennett’s design/build process will guide you through the steps of choosing the right design and materials to create your desired kitchen. Bennett partners with various local suppliers who have showrooms, samples and National Kitchen & Bath Association (NKBA) certified designers. Your kitchen is the heartbeat of your home; it needs to be both beautiful and functional. Here are some of things to look for when considering a contractor to remodel your kitchen:

Architectural plans when a remodel involves structural changes or enlarging the home
NKBA certified kitchen designer, with full CAD drawings of the layout and cabinetry
Plumbing fixture showroom accessibility for selecting fixtures, sink, faucet and accessories
Wide choice of cabinets, countertops and flooring
Tile, marble, ceramic designs and installation
Lighting design services
Full line of appliances and installation

With 100 years of experience, and thousands of completed jobs from handicap accessible to custom chef’s kitchens, Bennett can advise you each step of the way. Our licensed plumbers and electricians on staff work efficiently, meeting all the local codes and inspector requirements.

Porches & Decks
My front porch is in poor condition, what should I do?

Porches are complicated structures and their design is governed by a wide variety of codes and safety standards. Refer to the “how to select a contractor” section and then call a professional full service contractor like Bennett to set up a free consultation in order to identify what issues need to be addressed.

Porches in disrepair can pose risk and hazard to the homeowner and should not be ignored.
Many times older porches were built with inadequate footings, resulting in settling or sagging of the structure.
In certain cases where the roof is in good condition, the porch roof can be braced while new footings, columns, framing and decking are rebuilt below.
Wood rot is a very common problem with porches since they are exposed to the elements. This rot can result in a danger to the integrity of the structure.
The longer you neglect to repair or rebuild a porch, the worse the problem will get.
What Material should I select for my Deck Surface and Railings?

A deck’s structural framing is constructed with pressure-treated framing lumber and sits on steel or concrete piers.

The area of the deck that you walk on and the railings are available in a variety of materials including several grades and species of wood, modern composites and PVC (vinyl). Second only to the size of the deck, the choice of material will have the most effect on the purchase cost and future maintenance requirements.

Wood:

Pressure treated wood (southern yellow pine most common)
Available in standard (lower cost) and select grades (less knots)
Premium Species including Cedar, Mahogany and Teak
Higher cost, longer lasting, better looking.
All wood is higher maintenance. It is recommended to paint or stain the surface annually

Composite:

High cost, low maintenance
Wide variety of colors, and surfaces

PVC (vinyl)

High cost
Very low maintenance
Limited colors

A full service contractor like Bennett Contracting will help you design and create your ideal outside space while keeping in mind your budgetary restrictions.

Siding
Why Choose Vinyl Siding?

Beauty

While traditional pastel and earthy color options are still available, today’s vinyl siding offers a comprehensive array of darker color combinations including bold, rich tones like barn reds, hunter and sage greens, deep blues and more. Nearly 350 different colors are certified to meet the ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials) standards for vinyl siding color retention, so you can be sure the shades you select will resist major color changes in a variety of climates.

Durability

Of course exterior cladding has to look good for today’s discerning homeowners, but it also has a vitally important job of protecting a home from the elements. With the ability to withstand high winds (certified up to 110 mph or higher) and a composition that resists heat, cold and moisture, vinyl siding retains its great looks over time.

Vinyl siding never needs paint. Ever. The only maintenance it will need is a simple wash with a soft cloth and garden hose to keep it looking great, a feature today’s strapped-for-time homeowners really appreciate!

Green Building

Today’s vinyl siding, the most popular choice for exterior cladding in the United States and Canada, delivers recognized environmental benefits to help make and keep homes green.

Throughout the processes of manufacturing, transportation, installation, service life and waste management, vinyl siding scores well on tough environmental measures.  What’s more, vinyl siding has the potential to contribute to achieving more points than other exterior cladding in the leading green building certification programs including the United States Green Building Council (USGBC) LEED® for New Construction and LEED® Homes Rating Systems and the ANSI approved ICC 700-2008 National Green Building Standard™.

Choice

Any look – historic to contemporary – can be achieved with today’s vinyl siding. Vinyl siding has the widest array of profile offerings of any other cladding material including:

Horizontal and vertical panels
Shakes, Scallops, Shingles, Fish scales
Traditional lap
Dutch lap
Beaded designs in various profile widths

Today’s vinyl siding is available in a broad and ever increasing spectrum of solid and variegated colors. Dozens of new trim and accent options are also available to enhance neighborhood aesthetics. Vinyl siding is the number one choice for siding and Certain-Teed is the number one brand of siding.

How do I choose the right siding contractor?

One of the most important decisions you can make when it comes to fixing the exterior of your home is to hire a reputable siding company, like Bennett Contracting. While it might be tempting to take this project on by yourself, using a quality siding contractor can assure that your building products are installed correctly, avoiding any problems in the future from incorrect installation. To ensure you have a qualified siding installer, look for the following qualifications:

Certification: 

Your siding contractor should have skilled installers who have been trained by the manufacturer of the siding for your home.  Bennett employees are dual certified both be the Vinyl Siding Institute and Certain-Teed’s Five Star program. Beware of contractors who subcontract the installation.

Safety:

Your siding contractor should have the latest OSHA approved scaffolding and ladders, modern trucks and employees who have completed both OSHA safety and EPA Lead Safe Work Practice training. Your siding contractor should show you proof of insurances including worker’s compensation. Ask to see a certificate.

Choices, Designs, Referrals:

A quality siding contractor, like Bennett Contracting, has been around a long time and has hundreds of satisfied customers and completed homes like yours that you can look at.  You should also be able to view a computer rendering of your home to sample design choices. Look for siding contractor who offers options.  Insulation choices, such as blow-in cellulose, can make tremendous difference in your utility bills.

See How to choose a remodeling contractor for more general information.

How do I clean my vinyl siding?

How do I wash vinyl siding?
Wash vinyl siding with a soft cloth or ordinary long-handled, soft bristle brush. For textured surfaces, use only a soft bristle brush to keep the grooves in the texture stain-free. For best results, start at the bottom of the house and work up and rinse the cleaning solution completely before it dries.

Can I use a power washer?
Yes, though you should read the washer instructions carefully before use. When cleaning, hold the power washer straight at eye level to keep the water on top of the siding where it can clean most effectively. Do not aim the power washer upward as water may be driven behind the siding. Use caution around any opening in the wall, such as windows, doors, electrical wiring, and plumbing.

How do I remove mold and mildew?
Small spots of mold and mildew can be handled with cleaners such as Fantastik® or Windex®. For larger sections, a solution of vinegar (30%) and water (70%) has proven successful. Alternatively, you also could try the following solution: 1/3 cup (2 2/3 ounces) powdered laundry detergent (e.g., Tide®, Fab®, or equivalent), 2/3 cup (5 1/3 ounces) powdered household cleaner (e.g., Spic & Span®, Soilax®, or equivalent), 1 quart (32 fluid ounces) liquid laundry bleach, and 1 gallon (128 fluid ounces) of water.

What types of cleaners should I use for other stains?
A list of commonly accepted cleaners is provided in the box below. Be sure to spot check any general or stain specific cleaner before using it on a large section of siding. After removing the stain, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use cleaners containing organic solvents, undiluted chlorine bleach, liquid grease remover, nail polish remover, or furniture polish or cleaners. They can affect the surface of the siding.

Vinyl Siding Cleaners
General cleaners (e.g., Simple Green®, Nice & Easy®, Armor All®, etc.) can be used to clean dirt, bird droppings, and spider webs. Stain-specific cleaners are listed below. Rinse all cleaners with water before they dry.
Stain	Cleaners*
Bubble Gum	Fantastik®, Murphy Oil Soap®, solution of vinegar (30%), water (70%) and Windex®
Crayon	Lestoil®
DAP (oil-based caulk)	Fantastik®
Felt-tip Pen	Fantastik®, water-based cleaners
Grass	Fantastik®, Lysol®, Murphy Oil Soap®, Windex®
Lithium (car) Grease	Fantastik®, Lestoil®, Murphy Oil Soap®, Windex®
Motor Oil	Fantastik®, Lysol®, Murphy Oil Soap®, Windex®
Paint	Brillo® Pad, Soft Scrub®
Pencil	Soft Scrub®
Rust	Fantastik®, Murphy Oil Soap®, Windex®
Tar	Soft Scrub®
Top Soil	Fantastik®, Lestoil®, Murphy Oil Soap®
*Cleaning Materials are listed in alphabetical order.
*VSI does not endorse products or processes and makes no warranties for the products referenced herein. Reference to proprietary names is for illustrative purposes only and is not intended to imply that there are not equally effective alternatives.

 

WINDOWS/DOORS
How do I choose a quality window and door contractor?

Picking a high quality window is important. It helps ensure energy efficiency and insulation for your home.  Picking a high quality and experienced window installer is essential. High efficiency windows will not perform as designed unless they are correctly installed. Don’t be tempted to simply pick the contractor with the lowest price. The money you invested in the window could be wasted if they are not correctly installed.

Choices/Referrals

A full service window contractor will offer all types of windows and doors; wood, vinyl and metal from several manufacturers, to be able to select the product that best compliments your home. Beware of “one-size fits all” window companies who only sell one brand.
You should expect your contractor to have a fixed business location with a showroom, warehouse and service department.
Quality window contractors have been around a long time and will have many satisfied customers and homes like yours that you can go look at.
Windows and doors are components of your home and your installer should be versatile with carpentry skills and knowledge of construction.

Skills/Warrantee

A quality window installer has ongoing training programs or their employees and is certified by several window manufacturers.
Quality trades people are NOT piece-rate paid subs, they are hourly employees of an established local business.
You should receive two written warrantees, one from the installer for labor and one from the manufacturer covering the product.
Keep in mind that lifetime warrantees from companies that have only been in business a few years and not worth very much.

Safety

Your window contractor should have the latest OSHA approved scaffolding and ladders, modern trucks and employees who have completed both OSHA safety and EPA Lead Safe Work Practice training. Your window contractor should also show you proof of insurance, including worker’s compensation.  Ask to see a certificate.

See How to choose a remodeling contractor for more general information.

What type of material should I select for my replacement window?

Today’s windows are made of a combination of materials but generally fall into one of three categories: vinyl, wood or metal. Vinyl and wood are the two most popular for use in residential homes. What you are seeking from your windows in terms of budget, maintenance, look and function will help determine which style is right for your home.

Vinyl

Vinyl windows are the most popular because they are less costly, are available in many styles and require very little maintenance.
Vinyl windows are available in several forms:  double hung, casement, bay or bow, slider, garden, hopper and picture.
Bennett’s vinyl windows are manufactured in the Northeast from American made components.
All of the vinyl windows offered by Bennett Contracting come with a lifetime warrantee.

Wood

Wood windows are popular for their authentic look and feel. In historic areas wood is required, but in many older homes it’s just the right choice.
Wood windows are available with a low maintenance metal or vinyl cladding on the exterior.
Wood windows are available in a variety of woods including oak and pine for interior finishes.
Wood windows are available in several styles including: double hung, casement, bay, bow, hopper and picture.

Choices/Referrals:

A full service window contractor will offer all types of windows and doors including wood, vinyl and metal, from several manufacturers, to provide you with a selection of products that best compliments your home.
Beware of “one-size fits all” window companies who only sell one brand.
Quality window contractors have been around a long time and will have many satisfied customers and homes like yours that you can go look at.
Windows and doors are components of your home and your installer should be versatile with carpentry skills and knowledge of construction.
What Is A Change Order

Change Orders (CO’s) are the means by which we add, delete or modify the Work Schedule.

The Change Order form details the change in scope and the change in cost.

Here are some tips about change orders:

 

It’s OK: Don’t be scared of CO’s, they are normal and it is our way of documenting changes. It is very common for a project to have at least one change order. Larger jobs may have multiple change orders throughout the project’s duration.

 

Allowances: A specified dollar amount included in the price, which is how we budget for those materials that you need to select (ie tile). If you spend more than your allowance, the difference will be added plus sales tax. If you spend less, we credit the difference.

 

Adding: If you want to add work, just ask!!! The earlier the better, that way we can determine the impact on the job. It can be very cost effective to have our crew provide some added work while we’re already at your home working.

 

Modifications: Altering work can be tricky. If we’ve already ordered material based upon the original contract, and you request modifications, certain items may not be returnable. Also, if we have to re-do work that you’ve decided to change, we still need to charge for the labor and materials to do it again.

 

Time Frame: Adding or modifying work will result in the job taking longer. In some cases, if we have to wait for materials to arrive, we may even need to pull the crew off until the materials arrive and we can get back to work. Be prepared for these delays. Some Change Orders are out of our control and are just plain necessary.
Rot/Repairs: If we discover rot, it is necessary to fix it now. We will not ignore or cover up rot…it will only get worse and cost more down the road.
Code Upgrades: Most commonly with plumbing and electrical and especially in older homes. We always intend to include observable code upgrades, but we may discover hidden code violations inside the wall that require upgrades.
Surprise! Occasionally, we discover an unforeseen problem on a job. Maybe a cracked beam that was hidden. Be prepared for surprises.

 

Identify:  If possible, do a quick review with the Lead Carpenter each day.  If you would like to add work or make any modifications, first discuss with the Lead Carpenter to confirm if the change is possible and what might be involved. If necessary, the Project Manager or Designer will become involved with larger modifications.  Your Lead Carpenter may come to you with proposed changes (ie rot is discovered).

 

Communicating:  Once identified, in order to proceed, our Lead Carpenter will need your written or verbal authorization to do that additional work.  Be aware that if you agree to have additional work done, you are agreeing to pay for that work.  The Lead Carpenter will not offer to do extra work for free. Details of the added costs will be drawn up on a CO form for your review, either before the work is started or after (if Time & Material is used).

 

Pricing:  CO’s are either priced based upon Time & Material, or Lump Sum.  Either way, the price is determined based on materials, labor, subcontractors, taxes plus overhead and profit.  The rates and mark up percentages are spelled out on the Work Schedule.  The Project Manager and the Owner will determine which is used.

 

Conclusion:  You and Bennett are working together to create the project that you have imagined. We both want your job completed quickly, safely and with the best possible outcome.  In order to do that, we want to work with you in a collaborative manner. If changes are needed to reach that goal, we will work together to make that happen.

What Our Customers Have to Say!

We added a new bathroom. GARRETT WAS OUTSTANDING!! He was prompt, courteous, his ability to create everything was amazing. There was no job GARRETT couldn't handle. Congratulations to Bennett for hiring such an outstanding and honest individual. GARRETT IS TRULY THE BEST!

Had four vinyl windows replaced.  Had frames built out and wrapped with vinyl.  Steve came out to view the work that needed to be done.  He first thought that the frames holding the old windows were rotted, however, when Dean and Glen arrived and pulled the old windows out, they were not rotted, so I received a credit for not replacing the window frames.  Work was completed, however, because of a miscommunication, the windows were not framed in.  I called Steve and almost immediately, Glen arrived and framed the windows.  Work well done.  This company is great to work with!

Bennett Contracting replaced all of our windows and installed a sliding glass door about a year and a half ago.  They also took another sliding glass door out and put in a window as well as a wall where it was. It was a great experience.  They have excellent workmanship.  I would recommend them to anyone.  It was a good price and a lot less than some other groups that we had estimates from.  They were very nice to deal with and I will call them again.  They were great.

Put vinyl siding on detached 2-car garage.   Repaired/replaced a few dented pieces on existing aluminum siding on house.  Responded quickly to request for estimate.   Estimator very professional.  Took a few days for the estimate but the estimate was professionally done and the lowest estimate we received.   Other companies who gave us an estimate gave us an estimate on the spot but they were obviously "ball park" type estimates on their part and were higher than Bennett's. Bennett was able to do some trim work that other companies said couldn't be done (at least not by them).   They arrived on time and completed the work quickly to our satisfaction.   We understood that the estimate did not include costs of "lead paint safety" issues (a new law), and we did question the amount of those costs when they were added, but Bennett worked with us on that issue and it was satisfactorily resolved.

We needed to repair a 2-story back porch on a two family house.  Bennett came and reviewed what needed to be done and recommended that we replace everything.  We agreed that made the most sense and contracted with the company to replace the back porches.  It went extremely well.  We were originally planning to have the work done in late August or September.  Kevin called us and said they had an opening in their schedule if we wanted it done sooner.  We had the work done in July and it couldn't be better.  Not only do the porches look good, the materials are maintenance free and we won't have to worry about the porches again.  They were responsive to my concerns and made suggestions to make the project go smoothly.  Kevin was very good to work with and the carpenters were terrific - clean, professional, and easy to work with.  The site was cleaned up every day.  Everyone was pleasant and kept us informed each day of their progress.  We couldn’t be happier and will certainly use this company again.

Had a large deck installed by Bennett and we were completely satisfied with the work. The estimator did a great job taking in our ideas and added a few of his own. We chose composite decking material and we were completely satisfied with the outcome. We've had Bennett do other jobs for us and we experience the same level of superb craftsmanship each time. Highly recommend. Good experience working with these folks.

Contacted several contractors for an estimate on siding and gutters for our addition. Bennett had the best price, took the time to explain our options and made the process as easy as possible. Finished product still looks great a year out. Would definitely turn to them for future projects.

Hi guys, yes, we have used your fantastic company to add on an addition to our home. You had the whole job done in less than two months. Your guys were there everyday and the finished product was gorgeous! We only trust Bennett with our home. Thank you again for a job well done!

So ... Bennett just wrapped up a project at our home East of Albany. What started out as a possible siding job wound up as a complete window replacement, siding and roof replacement job and... minor bathroom renovation. Throughout the process, from the initial visit with Kevin Gutman to the men on site, the experience was a positive one. I strongly recommend Bennett for all of your renovation needs - Just started a fund for what I hope to be phase two come spring!

We just used Bennett for the first time to replace some fairly large windows my husband couldn't do himself. I am very impressed. We had gotten a few estimates and these guys seemed to have the best product for the best price. We also loved that the sales guy was in & out of our house unlike some other ones that stayed here for over an hour trying to sell us everything under the moon. The windows were put in yesterday & I can't believe how quick they were. The contractors were professional & skillful. If I ever need anything else done to the house I would call them again for sure.

We were in the process of having our bathroom re-done by Bennett when Hurricane Irene came along and complicated things by flooding our basement and leaving us without power. We were so impressed with the work John was doing on the bathroom, that we immediately called Bennett to arrange for them to take care of the damaged basement. The happy ending to the story is that both jobs came out beautifully!

Our estimator/project mgr Steve did a very good job explaining the process and giving a fair estimate.  He was there every step of the way to make sure I was happy with the work.  They moved patio doors from Kitchen to Dining room.  Walled up kitchen with new window and took down old porch off kitchen and put up new deck. The guys who did the work did a great job of getting to the house early every day.  They were able to answer every 'annoying homeowner' question and concern with no problems or judgment.  The job took a little over two weeks.  The workmanship on the deck was wonderful.  Every edge was routed down.  I haven't gotten to use it yet since it's been cold but it looks great!  They cleaned up everything and no detail was left untouched.  They even fixed the spring on my garage door (at no charge) that happened to break while they were working.  I'd definitely use them again.

Bennett Contracting provided estimate in June 2011 and then did work in September, working around my schedule. One carpenter, John, did most of the work including installation of the floor tile.  John brought in Bennett's plumber and electrician as needed.  Everything went smoothly from start to finish and consistent with the work schedule provided in June.  I was consulted when necessary and any questions I had as the work progressed were graciously answered.   All I can say is that everyone did the job asked of them and did it well.  Without exception they were all pleasant to deal with and performed professionally.  I would definitely hire them again.

We had siding put on the house by Bennett Contracting. He was here in September and they did the whole job in 2 weeks. They do all kinds of things. They were very good. There were here for 2 weeks and when they were here they were working and there was no fooling around. We got estimates from several places and that estimate was good. They were very punctual. They came everyday at the time they said they would and they worked all day. I think they were very professional. They had a supervisor who was there all the time. There were 3 guys and 1 guy was in charge and they took their lead from him.

Removed a fireplace and replaced it with a wall of windows; replaced a sliding patio door with french doors; replaced two leaky skylights with two ceiling windows; repaired roof; repaired siding; repaired gutter and downspout; installed additional vents in eaves for attic circulation. This was a story of persistence and ultimate success. Some snafus in the ordering process caused some delays, but overall the crew and management were fastidious in their attention to detail and quality. There were some surprises of long-term water damage when they removed the chimney, which meant that the project had to be expanded from the wall up into the ceiling. We negotiated this expansion at each point, and there were no problems. A door arrived with the active panel on the wrong side. Bennett was quick to re-order and even negotiated a discount for us, since the error occurred at the factory. We appreciated the integrity of both manager and crew. Reasonable price overall for the work they did. I'm very satisfied with the outcome. The crew did a wonderful job of trim and sanding, leaving me with perfect surfaces for staining and painting. I've scheduled additional work with this company.

Bennett replaced some rotted window trim on the back of the house and cloaked all the wooden trim on the exterior of the windows in aluminum. They were professional; the work was fairly priced, done in a day, and done well. I am thinking of hiring Bennett again this summer to do some insulation work and to give me a quote on upgrading my windows.

Excellent work Nick, Garrett, Patrick, and Bob. Wonderful attention to detail and would highly recommend Bennett as a contractor. Thank you.

Bennett just finished some work at my house, and I can't say enough about the fantastic work that they did with construction of a new overhang over my front door, and in rebuilding part of my deck. Patrick has a great attention to detail, deftly navigated some unforeseen surprises that popped up along the way, and kept me updated on status and his recommendations. Several neighbors have already noticed and complimented his work. I'm very pleased with everything that Bennett did and will definitely reach out to them again the next time I need work done.

We have been using Bennett for over 20 years and they have always provided excellent work, quality, trust and professionalism. Our recent front door installation was handled in a first class manner by Josh and Perry. Project support from Bryan and George was exceptional. Highly recommended!!

First , let me say that this company is a pleasure to deal with. We have had front and rear doors replaced, kitchen cabinet's moved to accommodate a larger fridge and now a new stainless drop in sink. this time our installer was Tony ( now to be our go to plumber) who was absolutely a pleasure to meet and have at our home. He was not only very considerate of our needs but kept me informed during the installation, to the very end of the job. He represents what a true craftsman should be and the type of talent Bennett has on staff. My wife and I couldn't be more pleased with our new sink..........

This project was a difficult structural repair of rotted wood on an outdoor “long house”. I was not sure if I could find someone to fix the rotted structural posts. Steve came over and reviewed and recommended Tom. Tom is a master craftsmen and artist in wood. They did an incredible job which I did not believe could be done!!

We are so happy with the bathroom renovation. David was very professional and always respectful of our home. Demolition of our bathroom was completed quickly and without dust and debris. The craftsmanship is impeccable and beautiful. I am very grateful for the team effort that went into the design, selection and installation. We will never go elsewhere for contracting work!

Very satisfied with Bennett's installation of a skylight in the stairwell of our 1847 built townhouse. Nice guys too!

I used the services of Bennett Contracting for insulation and window installation.  I last used them in the fall of 2010. They put in new insulation and replaced the window.  They did a really good job.  They were professional.  It did take some time, but they did the job.  They are pretty popular in the area.

I used them for my window replacement including 21 windows, a front door and a back door. They did fantastic job. They had a competitive price. They had professional staff and cleaned up everything when they left. There was no mess left behind.

Discovered a mold problem in attic. Caused by improper vent. Bennett knew exactly what needed to be done. Installed proper vents and I decided to add an optional attic fan. At the same time installed fan and vent unit in master bath. I have used Bennett in the past so I had high expectations. As usual they did everything in a timely and professional manner.

Two separate jobs (replaced windows and siding) around 2005 and 2006 approximately. My last contact was in 2009 for an estimate for bathroom renovation but we decided postpone the renovation. Great experience from the estimate, through selection of materials, visiting the showroom to see samples of both windows and siding, speaking with office staff, they were all very professional.

I called Bennett Contracting to install aluminum siding on my sun room. I had wood shake singles and the wood peckers found a home in the walls. They inspected my sun room to find water damage in the walls. This required replacement of the wall studs and and a new roof.  They furnished me a new estimate, which I agreed to, and proceeded with the work. The siding looks beautiful and complements the brick exterior of the main house.

We were very happy with Bennett. Both times we used them they were professional and very responsive to questions and concerns. The workmen were very punctual - work always began when we were told it would and the workers very, very diligent. They took a real concern in keeping the house clean and tried hard to minimize the disruption of the work to our family. We found their estimate was similar to ones we received from other contractors. We especially appreciated the willingness of the Bennett people to work with us in keeping costs down. We would definitely choose Bennett again.

Very professional and competent.  Offered ideas and suggestions and referred to suppliers who treated us with care and professionalism.  The workers who performed the actual work were craftsmen who took the time and patience to get the job done right and results were high quality.  The lead time for some smaller projects dragged out beyond our expected timeframe, but overall, we are extremely pleased with the results and would highly (HIGHLY) recommend Bennett to anyone looking to do simple, smaller jobs to larger remodels or additions.  The worksite was left clean and tidy each day; we experienced minimal interruptions; and, once the service date was established, the work was performed as scheduled.  Very reliable, responsive and competent!

We have a "Bennett House" because they did our siding, they did our windows, they rebuilt our front porch, they insulated our house, and they did repairs after a storm. I can only speak highly of them. I like that they clean up after themselves and that their work has been very competent. The men that have come out have been polite and I don't mind having them around. They would be the first ones that I would call.  We find that their prices are competitive and that we get what we pay for.

I've had many projects done by Bennett Contracting and I have never been disappointed. The quality of work on our bathroom and our screen room is outstanding. I've also had my house sided, a new front entrance, windows, lighting, ceilings done. You can't go wrong when using Bennett for home improvement projects.

Bennett Contracting did an excellent job re-siding and insulating our kitchen! We have a beautiful old brownstone and Bennett worked with the architecture of the building to make it all work! Wonderful job!

Great! The main contact, Kevin Gutman, was very professional and available.  Whenever I called Kevin with a question, he called back promptly.  The supply companies he worked with were also very professional.  We had no idea how to design a kitchen but Bennett helped us with all the decisions from appliances to countertops to plumbing.  Their workers were punctual and kept everything clean.  They also worked hard to make sure that everything worked the way it was supposed to and, even after the job was finished, came back the same day I called to fix a minor problem with the sink.  Because the work was over Christmas, we didn't get to make our usual Christmas cookies, so Dean, one of their carpenters, brought us a big tin of cookies that he made!  The window job was exactly the same.  Very nice workers who were punctual and made sure that every window worked well.  Very positive experience!

Bennett Contracting gutted our kitchen which included taking down a wall between the kitchen and dining room, pulling up linoleum floor, carpet, and hardwood flooring and moving windows along the back of the house They scraped off 3 rooms worth of popcorn on the ceiling and smoothed out the entire ceiling, installing can lights. They installed cabinets according to our layout, sub-floor and new tile floor, replicated and continued crown molding throughout the new layout. They installed pendent and under cabinet lighting and all the finishing touches we agreed upon. It took a couple of weeks longer than planned due to a change in our plans about flooring but they arrived daily and worked all day, leaving the workplace neat at the end of the day. The carpenter talked to us about the work and offered suggestions but always left the decisions to us. We were very pleased with the outcome and love the new kitchen. Our calls to the project manager were always returned the same day and our questions answered.

After quotes from several contractors we decided to hire Bennett to replace several double hung windows in our home. Although they were not the cheapest, the price was fair and the appraiser, Kevin, eased my concerns about preventing any lead/lead dust contamination as the home is old and we have a young child.  The 2 men, Jim and Carl, came on time and completed the work ahead of schedule and did a great job.  They even put a vent in and charged me nothing extra. We are very happy with the work and would hire them again. After the work we had the house inspected for lead dust by the department of health and they verified there was no contamination.

Bennett completely gutted the bathroom. They installed new ceiling, walls, floor, tub/shower, vanity, sink, toilet, door, lighting fixture. Did all Plumbing, electrical and tiling. We have used Bennett Contracting previously to remodel the kitchen. The same installers were assigned to do our bathroom. It was a 3 week project and the work progressed as scheduled each day. Bennett Contractors has been a professional and reliable company to work with.

From the first visit, we wanted this group. We hoped other estimates would come in higher so we would not be faced with a tough decision. We were not since Bennett's estimate was far lower than a company we had used before. Measurements (windows and siding) were taken to help with accurate estimate and re-taken even more precisely once the contract was agreed. When the materials were ready (about three-four weeks) work began. The crew was outstanding, especially Chris the manager. All were friendly and knowledgeable but, beyond that, totally professional in everything they did, an so hard working. They seldom stopped for a moment (did they even eat lunch??) Each day everyone arrived on time (Jared was 30 minutes early every day!) Materials were kept under control throughout the working day, cleaned and stored every evening. All questions were answered completely and in a very understandable way. When some old siding was removed it was revealed that there was a substantially dangerous situation with our electric wiring (due to another repair after a storm). The situation was explained very carefully to me, but the wheels for a safe and timely correction of the problem were already in motion by that time. Even the glitches seemed to run like clockwork with these people! When I showed some frustration at the way earlier repair (NOT by Bennett) must have been done, Chris explained why the other carpenter might have done it that way. Who knows, but I was impressed with his professionalism when he could have just as easily complained about the other guy. "Professionalism" was the name of the game with this crew. The house looks great. The windows work so well. The iron railing (an after thought on our part, but easily managed by Bennett, and cheaper than another estimate with lesser quality materials) finishes the whole project. Our only regret, was that we had not called them earlier for other work. We will definitely use this company again!

Bennett contracting was very easy to work with.  Workers were on time every day, were courteous, cleaned up the work site daily, answered all questions from customer, were very professional and did quality of work.

Bennett Contracting is always professional – willing to investigate any problems encountered/uncovered and make necessary repairs.  They replaced rotted garage door trim and rotted front door trim and investigated other water damage. Workers were knowledgeable and helpful.  Clean up was great.

The crews were impeccably prompt, professional, concerned to complete the job to the highest standards. Friendly and ready to explain everything.

Bennett Contracting personnel were punctual, professional, friendly, and ensured our satisfaction from initial estimate through completion of work.  A quality company with quality people.  I would highly recommend them.

My bathroom was completely gutted and redone. Work included radiant floor, spa type shower, tiling, painting, new toilet and vanity, ceiling heater/fan, etc. I also had a laundry room added to a first floor room. I was AWAY when this work was done and left complete instructions. They were followed meticulously and my house was in excellent order when I returned. This company is top of the line professional. I was given a lot of helpful advice by their "advance" man, who was able to understand my goals and he helped me achieve them. We were totally satisfied. The company had put protection over all my floors and did a complete clean up job so that you would not know they were even here - except we got a beautiful new bathroom and laundry room when we got back from Florida!

We had 3 estimates from different contractors to rebuild our home after a fire. Bennett came in with the most detailed bid, worked with us to avoid using an independent insurance adjuster (big expense) and have surpassed our expectations on the quality of the work. We had the entire house gutted and rebuilt including a complete reconstruction of the second floor. From the beginning the estimate came in quickly and was quite detailed. They even through in extras for free-remove a wall, change a window opening. The finishing work is being done now and it is better than the original builder. I would NEVER use anyone else. The work crew has become like family to us. We love them.

We just got our new windows installed today from Bennett and we love them! The service was professional from sales & selection to installation and they never pushed us into something we didn't want (which I can't say about other companies we talked to). We could not be happier with the product and the service! We would highly recommend Bennett to anyone. Can't wait for our new door tomorrow!

Replaced 39 windows, 2 storm doors and added vinyl siding and insulation to a sun porch.  House was built in 1920 and still had most of its original windows with 1950's-era aluminum storm windows.  Some of the window frames were rotted and all were painted with lead-based paint.  Bennett talked us out of using far more expensive wood frame replacement windows in favor of high quality vinyl frame windows.  Cosmetically, they are identical in appearance.  Bennett's carpenters did expert repairs to the rotted window frames in a very efficient manner that added little to the overall cost of the project.  The crew was very efficient and responsive and cleaned up the work area at the end of each day.  They did an outstanding job and I wouldn't hesitate to use them again. Estimates and detailed measurements were made at the end of July 2011.  Work was started in early October 2011 but was interrupted by extensive rain.  Crew needed inside access to remove the old windows and remove the lead-based paint.  This turned out to be less inconvenient than I originally feared as we generally only had to move furniture about three feet from the walls for access.  We allowed the crew to store project materials in our garage during the project.  Crew was very responsive to our requests including labeling 39 sets of original wood shutters.  Repairs to rotten wood were handled expertly and efficiently.  The crew also removed and replaced old insulation under the sun porch which proved difficult due to the extremely confined space.  They showed up in a timely fashion and left the work area clean at the end of each work period.  The end result was very noticeable in terms of heat retention and noise reduction - we about 50 yards from NY Rt 7. The final bill had no surprises.

We replaced 26 ancient windows with modern vinyl and wooden windows. We are happy with the windows. Their employees are professional. The window installers were very skilled and were considerate of us. I have no reservations about highly recommending them. From the beginning the estimate came in quickly and was quite detailed. They even through in extras for free-remove a wall, change a window opening. The finishing work is being done now and it is better than the original builder. I would NEVER use anyone else. The work crew has become like family to us. We love them.

Very pleasant professional experience from beginning to end.  Couldn't be happier with the result. Bennett ripped out and removed a set of pressure treated stairs with landing that was unstable and leaning away from the side of my raised ranch. Also replaced the side door to the stairs with a beautiful window, replaced outside vinyl house siding re: conversion from door to window, interior trim, drywall, and baseboard molding. Replaced a strip of dented vinyl garage molding and an outside electrical outlet cover as well. Attention to detail removed concrete stair footers along with the rest of the job, and had all completed in about 3 1/2 consecutive days.  My concern was that it was going to be messy and noisy, but I found no mess, and the noise was minimal and very tolerable.

I used Bennett Contracting Inc in last March. They did repairs in my bathroom, where there was a lot of water damage.  They did an excellent job. They communicated very efficiently and their estimate was correct. I would use them in the future.

We are extremely happy with the work Bennett did. They did a great job and my house looks amazing. Now I wish I could remodel the inside of the house to look as great as the outside. When that time comes we are definitely calling Bennett.

The job went smoothly and on schedule.   I had rotted exterior window framing, sills, and drip caps replaced on several windows and new framing around two doors constructed.   The job was well done and the work site was left clean. Bennett Contracting was very professional.  For a relatively small job they communicated with me several times, the salesman, Steve Drodzyk, came out to the site twice to meet with me, and the carpenter who actually did the job met with me once before beginning.  All my questions were answered and the work was fully explained.  I was not given the line, "Don't worry.  Just trust me.  It'll be fine," which I have heard many times before when I have asked questions.  I also received a quick response from the carpenter, Joe, when I had a question about the work he had performed.  He seemed to take pride in his work which is also becoming rare these days. I liked that Bennett adhered to state regulations, complying with lead regulations which other contractors I interviewed had not even mentioned.

Last year Bennett Contracting added a master suite, a laundry/bathroom, mudroom, basement, siding, insulation, and windows to our home. Each of the crews were on time, helpful, courteous, and cleaned up at the end of the day. The project was finished within the estimated time frame. We were very satisfied and would recommend Bennett.

Bennett Contracting did a bathroom remodel for us.  It included electrical, plumbing, construction, and all of that.  We are very happy with them; they are very responsive. We had them do several smaller jobs for us like rebuilding outdoor doorways and quickly doing some lighting for us.  They do the work well and they take their time.  I’m sure they could do speedy but we were looking for someone who was more careful than fast.  I really appreciated the extent to which they consulted with us as the job moved along.  They were very careful to discuss the options with us as things became apparent.  The manager checked in daily and the person primarily doing the work was careful and friendly.  I liked that the people working at my house all had great things to say about Bennett as an employer.  They had all been working for the company for a long time and they liked working for them.  They worked well as a team and I was very happy with them.  I thought the price was very reasonable and they were always here when they said they were going to be.

Bennett replaced all 14 windows, 2 sliding glass doors and 2 picture windows. The wrapping they applied to the outside of the windows is beautiful, they did an excellent job. At the beginning of each day they came in and told me what work was being done for that day and at the end of the day they cleaned up and came in to say good bye and what time they would be back the next day. They all were very nice and professional. They were finished when they said they would be and came in to show us how to work the windows. I would highly recommend Bennett Contracting to anyone...They won't disappoint....

We had two porches torn down and rebuilt this summer. The company and its staff were terrific to work with and we have had many compliments on the work that was done. We also hired Bennett to do work on the garage and install new doors. They went above and beyond our expectations. We will definitely hire Bennett Contracting again for future projects. They are professional, honest, and do excellent work. Thank you!

They are an A+ company all the way from the first quotes to the completed job. Bennett worked with us to stay in our budget. They installed 10 replacement windows. The product they sold is excellent, and it’s manufactured locally in Fonda NY. The installers went above and beyond to help us move furniture and other things as needed to complete the job. Other companies charge extra for these types of things. They were highly professional in all aspects. I highly recommend this company.  Workmanship was great too.

Thank you for making our dream come true.  Our new bathroom is beautiful.  We can understand why Bennett Contracting has been a respected and trusted business in the Capital District since 1915.  We felt a real connection with Steve D. and Chuck.  We appreciated the daily contact with Steve and Chuck and always knew our home was in good hands.  Chuck really cares and it is reflected in the work he does.  Steve was very helpful in coordinating the whole project and always keeping us informed.  We look forward to working with Bennett Contracting Inc. on future improvements to our home.  Great job!

Bennett replaced siding, windows, two sliding glass doors, new entry door, and rebuilt front porch. Great experience. Crew was professional and courteous.  Showed up when scheduled and on time.  Work was done to my satisfaction.  Work area was cleaned up every day.
Contact Us

service@bennettcontracting.com

Professional Kitchen Remodelers in Albany, NY

Your kitchen is one of the most important spaces in your home—it should be both functional and inviting. A thoughtful renovation can transform your kitchen into a stylish, comfortable, and efficient space that meets your family’s needs and reflects your personal taste.

Is It Time to Update Your Kitchen?

Normal wear and tear, such as cracked tiles, persistent leaks, or mold, is often the first sign that your kitchen needs a remodel. Other key reasons to renovate your kitchen include:

Upgrading to meet your family’s needs
Boosting your home’s resale value
Upgrading to fit your personal style
Increasing energy and water savings
Improving functionality and eliminating inconvenience

Work with a trusted local contractor, Bennett Contracting, who understands Upstate New York homes and ensures every kitchen remodel is completed with care, precision, and attention to your unique needs.

Request a Quote
Benefits of a Kitchen Remodel in New York's Capital Region

Planning a kitchen remodel comes with many benefits:

Upgraded appliances: New, high-performing appliances make cooking safer, faster, and more efficient, helping you tackle daily kitchen tasks like a pro.
More workspace: Remodeled countertops provide a bigger, cleaner workspace, making meal prep and entertaining easier.
Increased storage: Updated cabinets and smart storage solutions keep your kitchen organized and clutter-free while maintaining a sleek look.
Boost home value and appearance: Kitchen renovations enhance your home’s style and value. Even minor updates, like new countertops or backsplashes, can make your entire home shine.
Long-term savings: Energy-efficient appliances, lighting, and fixtures help reduce utility costs, allowing you to save money over time.

Ultimately, a kitchen renovation should reflect your needs, lifestyle, and the condition of your space. Working with Bennett Contracting ensures your remodel is handled smoothly and enhances your home’s style, functionality, and value.

Request a Quote
Why Work with Bennett for Your Next Kitchen Remodel Project?

At Bennett Contracting, we don’t just remodel kitchens; we transform your space to combine style, comfort, and functionality, delivering every project with precision and care. Here’s why homeowners in New York’s Capital Region have trusted our local, family-owned business since 1915:

Quality brand-name products and guarantees
Professional, highly skilled carpenters and craftsmen
Best-in-class training and safety measures
Superior customer service and communication
Accurate and timely estimates

We set the bar high, delivering the quality service and workmanship our customers have come to rely on. Plus, we’re consistently recognized as the Times Union’s Best of the Capital Region, Daily Gazette’s Best of the Best, Nextdoor Neighborhood Fave, NAHB SAFE Award winner, and Remodeler of the Year by the Capital Region Builders & Remodelers Association. We also do bathroom remodels.

What we build

Renovation, done end to end

Design, permitting, construction, and finish work under one roof. Six specialized crews. One project manager per home, start to walkthrough.

From $75K
Kitchen remodeling
Full gut renos, layout reworks, and additions. Custom cabinetry, stone counters, integrated appliance plans. Cabinet orders go in the week your selections are signed, so the long-lead item is never the thing holding up your build.
Explore kitchens
From $40K
Bathroom renovation
Primary suites, wet rooms, half baths. Heated floors are not a luxury in a Michigan February, they are the reason you stop dreading the tile. Every shower pan gets a flood test before anything goes on the wall.
Explore bathrooms
From $70K
Basement finishing
Family rooms, home theaters, in-law suites, wet bars. We check the perimeter drain, the sump, and the grade outside before we frame a single wall down there. A bedroom needs a code-compliant egress window, and we cut it.
Explore basements
From $185K
Home additions
Second-story builds, primary suite additions, ADUs, in-law suites. Engineered drawings and full permitting handled. In-law suites with a first-floor bath are the fastest-growing request we get across all six counties.
Explore additions
From $45K
Decks and outdoor
Composite and hardwood decks, three-season rooms, covered patios. Footings go below the frost line and framing gets sized for snow load, not just for the seventy-degree day it was built on.
Explore outdoor living
From $350K
Whole-home renovation
Down-to-studs rebuilds, historic restoration, full-floor reworks. Phased construction so your family stays in-home when possible, with one schedule covering every trade. On the Craftsman and Victorian stock around Ann Arbor we mill trim profiles to match what is already in the house, not the closest thing on a shelf.
Explore whole home

Service area

Everything inside an hour of the shop

Six counties, all dispatched from one building on Platt Road in Ypsilanti. We drew the line at about an hour because a crew that leaves at 6:45 should be working by 8:00, not sitting on I-696. Each county runs its own permit timelines and its own inspectors, and we hold the license in all six. See every project we have finished.

Washtenaw County
Headquarters
Home base. The Ypsilanti shop, the design studio, and the largest concentration of finished work. Historic review on the Old West Side, straightforward everywhere else.
Wayne County
25 min
Plymouth out to Livonia and Belleville. Mostly 1950s ranches and 1920s downtown blocks, which are two completely different jobs on the same street grid.
Oakland County
45 min
Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Royal Oak. The premium market our six-figure builds were designed for, and the one place where design review can add a month.
Livingston County
30 min
Lake homes, hobby farms, and full additions in and around Brighton. Shoreline lots bring their own setback and septic conversations.
Monroe County
25 min
Lakeshore properties and the Toledo-edge market. Floodplain checks come up more often here than anywhere else we work.
Macomb County
55 min
Sterling Heights, Shelby, and the lake-adjacent neighborhoods east of I-94. Our longest haul, so we schedule these in blocks rather than one-off days.

Southeast Michigan housing stock

What we find behind the walls

The year your house was built predicts most of your budget. We have opened walls in every one of these eras, in every one of these neighborhoods, and the surprises stopped being surprises a long time ago. Find your house below and you will know what we are looking for before we get there.

Before 1920
Balloon frame and plaster

Ann Arbor's Old West Side and Water Hill. Ypsilanti's Normal Park and Depot Town. Downtown Plymouth and Northville. Grosse Pointe's older blocks.

Knob-and-tube wiring still live in a ceiling box
Plaster and lath over rough-sawn studs on irregular centers
No subfloor insulation, and often no subfloor
Galvanized supply lines choked down to a pencil
A coal chute bricked into the basement wall

Exterior changes inside Ann Arbor's historic districts go to the Historic District Commission before they reach the building department. Budget four to eight weeks for that review, and design to it from the start rather than appealing later.

1920s to 1940s
Brick bungalows and colonials

Royal Oak, Berkley and Ferndale's brick bungalow grid. Birmingham's older colonials. Dearborn and the Wayne County streetcar blocks.

Cast-iron waste stacks, sometimes scaled half shut
Sixty-amp service in a fuse box behind a door
Arched plaster openings worth every hour it takes to save
One original bathroom, five feet by seven
Solid oak floors under three layers of vinyl

These are the best bones in the region. The kitchens are small because 1928 wanted them small, and opening one to the dining room is almost always a load-bearing conversation. A flush beam and two point loads to the basement is the usual answer in the Royal Oak bungalow blocks.

1950s to 1970s
Ranches and split-levels

Livonia, Westland, Canton and Belleville. Warren and Sterling Heights out through Macomb. Southfield and the older Farmington streets.

Copper supply, which is the good news
Aluminum branch wiring in houses built about 1965 to 1973
Original single-pane aluminum sliders
Undersized returns, so the back bedroom never warms up
A load-bearing center wall a beam can usually replace

Eight-foot ceilings make these feel smaller than they are. Pulling the center wall and running the ceiling flat changes the whole floor for less than most people expect. If we find aluminum branch circuits, they get pigtailed with approved connectors and that line item goes in the proposal, not a change order.

1980s to 2000s
Big footprints, tired finishes

Novi, Northville Township, South Lyon and Brighton. Rochester Hills, Troy and West Bloomfield. Saline and Pittsfield's newer subdivisions.

Builder-grade oak everywhere, in good structural shape
Two-story foyers that owners now want closed in
Original decks at the end of their service life
Polybutylene or early CPVC in a narrow band of builds
Whirlpool tubs nobody has filled since 2009

Structurally these are the easiest houses we work on, which means the money goes where you can see it. The common project in the Novi subdivisions and the Rochester Hills builds is a kitchen and primary bath together, because the layouts are already right and the finishes are twenty-five years old.

How it works

Four phases. No surprises.

From the first call to final walkthrough, every project runs on the same documented process. You always know what comes next, and you always know who to call.

01
 / 04

One project manager owns your house from contract to warranty visit. Not a rotating cast, not a dispatcher. The same person who walked your basement in February is the one handing you the care guide in May.

Week 1
Discovery call

A working conversation about scope, budget, and what you actually want the space to do. We will tell you on that call if your number and your wish list do not meet. No sales pressure, and no reason to be polite about it.

Weeks 2–3
Design and proposal

In-home measure, 3D renderings, materials selection, and a fixed-scope proposal with real numbers. You see the room before you commit to it, and you see every line item that adds up to the total.

Build phase
Construction

Zip-wall barriers up, ram board down, photos in JobTread every day so you can check the site from a meeting. Your home stays livable wherever we can manage it, and we tell you straight when we cannot.

Final week
Walkthrough and warranty

Punch list, final inspection, care guide, warranty packet. The one-year visit goes on the calendar before we pull the last truck off your driveway, so nobody has to remember to schedule it.

See the full process

Wright's Repairs

Have a smaller project in mind? Let's chat!

Most people assume a company that frames additions will not come out to rehang a door. For three years they were right. We turned down hundreds of homeowners who had already hired us for something bigger, because a two-hour job does not fit inside a twelve-week build.

Wright's Repairs is what we did about it. Its own technicians, its own van, its own schedule, and the same builder's license and finish standard that stands behind a six-figure kitchen. More than sixty jobs, each written out on a page of its own with the scope, the limits and what moves the price.

See the full repair catalog
Call (734) 251-4187
What a repair visit looks like

The same paperwork as a kitchen, on a job that takes an afternoon

Quote
Priced from photos and a short video, in writing, before anyone drives out
Ceiling
A not to exceed figure. Nothing goes past it without your written OK
Who comes
A Wright's employee in a marked van, named in your confirmation text
After
Before and after photos on the invoice, and one year on workmanship
One
One thing broke

A toilet running all night, a cracked ceiling, a deck board gone soft underfoot, a deadbolt that stopped turning. Send photos and a few seconds of video, get a written range and a ceiling, then get a date. No morning lost to an estimate visit.

Two
A list you have been saving up

Most people call with five or six things at once, and that is the shape that works best for both sides. Twenty packages bundle the ones that tend to arrive together: a move, a new baby, an inspection report with fourteen items, the first hard freeze.

Three
The job that turns out to be bigger

Sometimes a patch visit finds a remodel. Three failing fixtures in one bathroom is a renovation argument, not a repair one. The crew that would quote it works in the same building, so nothing gets diagnosed twice and the handoff costs you nothing.

bathroom fixtures and tile
doors, locks and hardware
drywall, plaster and texture
baseboard, shelving and railings
deck boards and railings
squeaks, gaps and floor patches
sashes, balances and glazing
one room, one ceiling, one stairwell
cabinet doors and drawer slides
fixtures, fans and lanterns
valves, traps and supply lines
downspouts and storm damage
the twenty repair packages

Repairs runs a tighter radius than our renovation crews, about thirty minutes by road from the shop at 7101 Platt Road in Ypsilanti. Outside that ring, ask anyway and you will get a straight answer.

Who you actually work with

A company small enough that the founder still answers the phone
Design before demolition

Most contractors treat design as a step they have to get through. We treat it as the work. Before a single wall comes down you will see 3D renderings, signed-off material specs, and a fixed-scope build calendar. It is the heart of our design-build method.

It costs more time upfront. It costs less in change orders, surprise budgets, and the regret of finishing a project and realizing the layout still does not quite work.

Built for the long version of the story

Trends are easy. A space that still feels right in twelve years is harder. We pull from the era of the house, the bones of the neighborhood, and the way you actually live now to find the version that ages well.

That is why we say no to certain finishes, even when clients ask for them. If a choice is going to look dated before the warranty runs out, you will hear it from us first. Honesty is part of the work.

The kitchen that gets remodeled twice in twenty years is more expensive than the one designed correctly the first time. Our entire job is making sure you only do this once.

Founder and CEO. Started the company at 19 with one pickup truck in 2021.

WS

Joined in 2021. Runs the discovery calls and the proposal you will actually sign.
PM
Your project manager
One per house, start to finish
Assigned at contract. In your JobTread portal daily. More about the team.
01
Honest budgets

Real numbers, before the contract. No bait pricing, no figuring it out as we go.

02
One project manager

A single point of contact from contract to final walkthrough. You always know who to call.

03
House stays livable

Dust barriers, floor protection, daily cleanup. Wherever we can keep you in-home, we do.

04
Permits pulled

Every job, every time. We are the ones at the building department, not you.

Why six-figure clients choose us

Same scope, same Michigan market. Here is what changes when you hire a design-build firm instead of a general contractor. See how our process works.

Design-build in Southeast Michigan
One team plans it. The same team builds it.

Most renovations split design and construction between two companies that have never met. Wright’s Renovations does both under one roof, one contract, and one phone number you call when you have a question.

Start your project
See our work
one
team

Designer, project manager, and crew sit on the same side of the table.

one
contract

A single agreement covers drawings and the build. No handoff.

one
number to call

When something comes up, you already know who answers.

What design-build means
The plans and the build answer to the same people.

In the older way of working, you hire a designer to draw your kitchen remodel, then take those drawings out to contractors for bids. The designer never sees a job site. The builder never sat in your first meeting. When the framing meets the drawing and they disagree, you are the one stuck between them.

Design-build closes that gap. The people who price the work helped draw it, so the budget you approve is the budget that gets built.

That single line of accountability is the whole point. A wall that costs more to move than expected gets flagged during design, on paper, before anyone swings a hammer. The same logic carries through every service, from a bathroom renovation to a full home addition.

How a project moves
a
We sit down together

Goals, budget, and the parts of your house that drive you up the wall.

b
We design and price as one step

Every drawing carries a real number, not a placeholder.

c
We build what you approved

Same team, daily photos, the schedule you signed off on.

d
We walk it with you

You sign off on the finished room, not a punch list of excuses.

One team. One contract. One number to call.
The honest comparison
The split approach versus design-build

Both can produce a good room. The difference is who carries the risk when the drawing and the job site disagree.

 
Design, then bid, then build
Design-build with Wright’s
Who is accountable
Designer and builder point at each other
One team owns the whole outcome
When you learn the real cost
After drawings are done and bids come back
During design, on every decision
How phases run
Each one waits for the last to finish
Design and prep overlap, so you start sooner
Your paperwork
Separate contracts with each company
A single contract with clear terms
When problems surface
On site, as expensive change orders
On paper, before the build begins
Why it works for you
What the single line of accountability actually buys

The structure is plumbing. These are the things you notice while living through a renovation.

You start sooner

Because design and pre-construction overlap, prep begins before the last drawing is signed.

The budget holds

Costs are attached to choices while you are still choosing, so the final number rarely surprises you.

One person knows everything

Your project manager has the same dashboard you do. No re-explaining your house to a stranger.

The ideas are buildable

Designs are checked against framing, plumbing, and code as they are drawn, not after they are approved.

Fewer surprises mid-build

The hard questions get answered during design, where changing your mind costs an eraser, not a demo crew.

One schedule, kept honest

The same team that drew the timeline is the team building to it, so a slip in one phase is caught in the next.

The
process
Four phases, one team

You always know which phase you are in and who to ask about it.

phase one
Discovery

We learn the budget, the timeline, and what the space needs to do that it does not do now.

phase two
Design and price

Drawings and dollar figures grow together, so you approve a plan you can actually afford.

phase three
Build

Daily photos, a live schedule, and one project manager from demo to the last coat of paint.

phase four
Walkthrough

We go room by room together, fix anything you flag, and hand over a space that matches the plan.

Built for Michigan houses
We only build here.

Working one region deep means we already know the soil, the permit desks, and the way a 1920s Ann Arbor foundation behaves in February. A firm flown in from out of state finds that out on your dime. Explore our full range of remodeling services or see what we do in Macomb County and beyond.

Climate-aware design

Plans that account for Michigan’s freeze-thaw swings and humidity, not a generic spec sheet.

Older-home know-how

Updates that respect a house’s original character while bringing it up to how people live now.

Permit relationships

Standing familiarity with building departments across all six counties we serve.

Local ground truth

What the soil and water table mean for foundations, drainage, and basement finishing.

Home remodeling, planned as one house.

Most remodels start with one room and spill into the next. Wright’s Renovations draws the whole house first, then builds it in one order with one crew. The kitchen, the baths and the basement finish like they belong to the same home. It’s home remodeling for Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti and the towns around them, run out of one building on Platt Road.

Contact us now for a free quote

Why a whole home remodel runs better on one plan

Four rooms remodeled one after another rarely add up to one house. Kitchens, bathrooms and basements share wiring, plumbing stacks and framing, so the order they’re built in decides how many times a wall gets opened. Wright’s maps the entire house first, then sets that order. Phasing a whole-home renovation follows the same rule: the plan comes first, and the phase lines get drawn on top of it.
